newsitem.title: USA: NASD seen unlikely to waive muni rule for firm.
newsitem.headline: NASD seen unlikely to waive muni rule for firm.

text.p: The NASD is unlikely to grant Morgan Stanley & Co, a unit of Morgan Stanley Group Inc, a waiver permitting it to continue to do negotiated bond business with Massachusetts after one of its bond executives gave a $1,000 political contribution to the state's governor, an NASD official said on Tuesday.
"I don't think there will be a waiver granted," said the National Association of Securities Dealers official, who asked not to be identified.
NASD only grants such waivers if "there is an extremely good reason for the violation," he said in a telephone interview with Reuters.

The NASD official's comments came after Morgan Stanley announced that Peter Karches, head of the firm's fixed-income department, contributed to Massachusetts Governor William Weld's U.S. Senate campaign.
Morgan Stanley said in a one-page statement on Monday that Karches did not realize contributions to state or local officials running for federal office can be covered by rule G-37.

It added that the firm has withdrawn from any negotiated bond business with Massachusetts authorities while NASD reviews a request by the firm for a "waiver" from the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board's "pay-to-play" rule G-37.
Enacted by MSRB in April 1994, rule G-37 bars municipal dealers that make contribution to issuer clients from doing business for two years with those governments.
The NASD has authority to grant exemptions from the rule under criteria developed by the association and MSRB.
Reid Walker, associate director of media relations for NASD, had no comment on Morgan Stanley's request for a waiver.
He noted, however, that NASD is granting exemptions only under very limited circumstances.
"All we can say is we haven't granted a waiver all year," Walker said.
